limitations: Probe drawn from a random policy: it matches random's experience distribution, which if anything favors random — a conservative test for AI. Identical init across modes makes probe-before identical by construction. 3 seeds; affect='none'.

preregistered.ablation: The action policy (active_inference vs greedy vs random).
preregistered.baseline: arch_b with action_mode greedy / random (same world model, same seeds — only the act() policy differs).
preregistered.hypothesis: Active-inference action selection produces larger uncertainty reduction than greedy/random, measured as probe-set prediction-error decline (not error decline within predictable regions).
preregistered.kill_rule: AI seed-mean IG_probe <= max(greedy, random) seed-mean IG_probe -> label stays off PERMANENTLY (NR-B-009).
preregistered.metric: IG_probe = mean|e0| on a FIXED probe set before − after 15-episode pomaze training; seed-meaned. Secondary: mean_return.
preregistered.null: AI probe-error reduction <= greedy/random — the IG term is not causal; the 'active inference' label stays off permanently.
preregistered.procedure: Probe: 400 transitions from random-policy pomaze rollouts (fixed seeds, policy-independent). Per (seed, mode): fresh agent with IDENTICAL init across modes -> probe-before -> 15 closed-loop episodes -> probe-after. Probe eval is pure model prediction (eval_transition: no memory store, no retrieval correction) — it measures model knowledge, not memory.
